💱 The rand has slipped from about R16.53 to about R17.55 to the dollar in nine days. Here's what that means for your money.

⛽ Fuel: oil is priced in dollars. A barrel of Brent at $90 cost about R1,488 at R16.53, and about R1,580 at R17.55. That's roughly 6% more in rand.

📱 Imports: anything priced in dollars costs more. A $500 phone goes from about R8,265 to about R8,775 before taxes and shipping.

🛒 Food: dearer fuel raises transport costs, which feed into what we pay at the till over time.

🏦 Rates: inflation is already 5.2%. A weaker rand can push it higher, and that's what the Reserve Bank watches when it sets interest rates.

The good news: the rand moves both ways. If it firms, these costs ease.

General information, not financial advice.

🛍️ "Pay later" on Black Friday: four questions before you tap.

Buy now, pay later (BNPL) splits a purchase into instalments, often four, and is usually advertised as interest-free if you pay on time.

1️⃣ What's the total? Add up all the instalments, and any fees.
2️⃣ What if I miss a payment? Check the late fees and what happens to your account.
3️⃣ How many am I running? Several small plans can add up to one big monthly bill in January.
4️⃣ Is it a need or a want? A deal on something you didn't plan to buy isn't a saving.

General information, not financial advice.

Have you used "pay later" before? How did it go? 👇

🧾 Black Friday: know your rights before you buy.

🔹 Faulty goods: under the Consumer Protection Act, you can return defective goods within six months for a repair, replacement or refund (your choice, within the rules).
🔹 Online shopping: the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act gives you seven days after delivery to cancel most online purchases. You may have to pay the cost of sending it back.
🔹 "No refunds" signs don't override your right to return faulty goods.
🔹 Keep your slip or proof of payment, even on a small purchase.

Not happy? Go back to the shop first, then the Consumer Goods and Services Ombud or the National Consumer Commission.

General information, not legal advice.

Have you ever had to return something you bought on special? 👇

🚨 Festive season scams: five to watch for this December.

1️⃣ Fake delivery SMSes asking you to "pay a small fee" through a link.
2️⃣ "Too good to be true" online deals on social media, with payment by EFT only.
3️⃣ Calls from "your bank" asking for an OTP or PIN. Your bank will never ask for these.
4️⃣ Fake job offers that ask you to pay an "admin fee" first.
5️⃣ Investment schemes promising big, guaranteed returns before Christmas.

If in doubt: hang up, don't click, and call your bank on the number on the back of your card.

Please share this with your family group. 🙏

#MzansiMoneyMatters #ScamAlert #Fraud
